title: A stable nonanuclear Tb(III) cluster for selective sensing of picric acid

synthesis.procedure: Acetylacetone (1.0 mmol, 0.100 g) was added to a methanol solution (10 mL) of TbCl3·6H2O (0.5 mmol, 0.186 g) and stirred for 10 min. Triethylamine (2 mmol, 0.202 g) was added dropwise and the mixture was stirred at room temperature for 48 h, then filtered on Celite. The filtrate was evaporated under vacuum. The white solid (67.6% yield; 2.22 g, 0.67 mmol) was recrystallized from methanol, and colourless crystals suitable for X-ray analysis were obtained at room temperature by slow evaporation.
synthesis.time: 10 min then 48 h stirring; crystallization by slow evaporation
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution stirring; Celite filtration; vacuum evaporation; recrystallization from methanol
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered on Celite; filtrate evaporated under vacuum; white solid recrystallized from methanol; colourless crystals by slow evaporation at room temperature

properties.summary: Complex 1 is highly luminescent, showing green Tb(III) emission under UV excitation in methanol and in the solid state. It selectively senses picric acid among nitroaromatics by fluorescence quenching, including in saturated PA vapour, and can be reused over several cycles.

measurements.name: excitation wavelength
measurements.conditions: methanol solution of 1 at room temperature

measurements.name: emission maxima (5D4→7F6,5,4,3)
measurements.conditions: MeOH; most intense 546 nm (5D4→7F5) responsible for green luminescence

measurements.name: photoluminescence quantum yield
measurements.conditions: relative to sodium salicylate (φ=0.55) in water; 1 measured in methanol

measurements.name: fluorescence quenching efficiency toward picric acid
measurements.conditions: 1×10−5 M 1 in MeOH titrated with 1×10−3 M PA; ~200 μL PA; 546 nm band

measurements.name: quenching constant (k) toward PA
measurements.conditions: nonlinear Stern–Volmer/exponential fit of F0/F vs [PA] in MeOH

measurements.name: thin-film quenching efficiency toward saturated PA vapour
measurements.conditions: thin film of 1 on quartz; 420 s exposure
